subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following pair of compounds are geometrical isomers?

image.alt: Four pairs of structural diagrams (A, B, C, D) showing potential geometrical isomers. Option B shows cis/trans but-2-ene pair.

explanation:
For two alkenes to be geometrical (cis-trans) isomers, they must be the same compound (same molecular formula and connectivity) with each double-bond carbon carrying two different groups, differing only in spatial arrangement around the C=C bond.

Option A: Left is but-2-ene, right is propene — different compounds. ❌

Option B: Left is trans/E-but-2-ene (CH₃ groups on opposite sides). Right is cis/Z-but-2-ene (CH₃ groups on same side). Same formula (C₄H₈), same connectivity, only spatial arrangement differs — genuine geometrical isomers. ✅

Option C: Right structure has two identical CH₃ groups on one carbon — no cis/trans possible; also a different compound (2-methylpropene). ❌

Option D: Right structure has an ethyl group (C₂H₅) making it pent-2-ene, not but-2-ene — different compounds. ❌

Therefore, option B is the only pair of genuine geometrical isomers.

(d) Give the major products of the following reactions:
(i) C6H5COCl → (LiAlH4) ?
(ii) C2H5CONH2 + NaOH → ?
(iii) CH3COCH3 + CH3COCH3 → ?
modelAnswer:
(i) C₆H₅CH₂OH (benzyl alcohol).
(ii) C₂H₅COONa + NH₃ (sodium propanoate + ammonia).
(iii) (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂COCH₃ (diacetone alcohol / 4-hydroxy-4-methylpentan-2-one).
